question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>z</mi></mfenced></math> represent the principal argument of the complex number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math>. The, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="|" open="|"><mi>z</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>arg</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mi>arg</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> intersect:

solution.text:
Let z represent the principal argument of the complex number z.

The, z=3 will represent a circle with centre 0,0 and radius 3 units

And  argz-1-argz+1=π4 will represent arc of the circle with centre 0,1 and radius 2, now on plotting the diagram,

     

We can see they are intersecting nowhere.
